_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Nauru covering Micronesian/Polynesian settlement (~1000 BCE), 12 original tribes (12-pointed star on flag), German annexation (1888), phosphate discovery (1900), mandate to Australia/UK/NZ, WWII Japanese occupation (1942-45, 1,200 Nauruans deported to Chuuk), independence 1968, phosphate wealth boom (1970s-80s highest per capita income), phosphate exhaustion and economic collapse, Australian offshore detention centre (2001-present, asylum seekers, Pacific Solution).

religion.note: Nauru Congregational Church (largest, 35%, London Missionary Society legacy); Catholic (~33%, Sacred Heart missionaries); Assemblies of God; Nauru Independent Church; Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints; traditional beliefs extinct; Sunday observance; church is primary community institution

ethnic_groups.name: Nauruan
ethnic_groups.notes: Micronesian/Polynesian mixed; 12 original tribes (represented by 12-pointed star on flag); distinct language (Nauruan, language isolate within Micronesian); matrilineal elements; phosphate royalties (1970s-80s wealthiest per capita on Earth, squandered on bad investments including London musical Lydia!, trust funds depleted); now among poorest; obesity crisis (97% overweight, highest in world, diabetes epidemic, imported food dependency, traditional diet abandoned); communal culture

ethnic_groups.name: Kiribati (I-Kiribati)
ethnic_groups.notes: Phosphate workers brought during British/Australian administration; distinct community

ethnic_groups.name: Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Tuvaluan, Filipino (worker migrants), Australian (detention centre staff), European; asylum seekers in detention (Australian offshore processing, variable population, not counted as residents)

country_profile.notes_unique: Smallest republic in world (21 km², 3rd smallest country after Vatican/Monaco); phosphate boom and bust (bird guano phosphate deposits mined from 1907, British Phosphate Commission then Nauru Phosphate Corporation, 1970s-80s highest per capita GDP on Earth ~$50k, Nauruans didn't have to work, invested in Melbourne real estate/London musicals/failed businesses, trust fund squandered, phosphate 80%+ exhausted by 2000s, interior of island is 'Topside' moonscape/coral pinnacles, 80% of land mined out, uninhabitable, environmental devastation, cautionary tale of resource curse); Australian offshore detention (2001 Pacific Solution, 2012 reopened, asylum seekers processed on Nauru, ~1,200 at peak, human rights abuses documented, mental health crisis, children detained, Amnesty/UNHCR condemnation, major revenue source for Nauru ~15-25% GDP, morally controversial); obesity epidemic (97% adults overweight, 71% obese, world's highest rates, Type 2 diabetes ~40%, imported processed food dependency, traditional fishing/gardening abandoned during phosphate wealth, public health crisis); WWII Japanese occupation (1942-45, 1,200 of 1,850 Nauruans deported to Truk/Chuuk, forced labour, 463 died, 2/3 population loss); no official capital (Yaren de facto, no cities, whole island is effectively one community); single oval road (island circumnavigation 19km); used as money laundering haven (1990s-2000s, 400+ shell banks, FATF blacklisted, international pariah, cleaned up); ICJ phosphate case (Nauru v Australia 1992, phosphate rehabilitation); parliament 19 members (one of smallest); weightlifting (disproportionate success at Commonwealth Games relative to population)

current_leader.name: David Adeang
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Elected by Parliament; former finance minister; long-serving MP; detention centre financial management; switched diplomatic recognition from Taiwan to China (January 2024, economic incentives); development focus

former_leaders.name: Russ Kun
former_leaders.notes: Brief tenure; succeeded Aingimea; unstable parliamentary politics

former_leaders.name: Lionel Aingimea
former_leaders.notes: Lawyer; human rights background; detention centre management; COVID response (kept virus out); Taiwan recognition maintained

former_leaders.name: Baron Waqa
former_leaders.notes: Authoritarian tendencies; suppressed opposition; expelled NZ judge; media restrictions; Australian detention centre expansion; controversial

former_leaders.name: Marcus Stephen
former_leaders.notes: Olympic weightlifter (3-time Olympian, remarkable for 21km² nation); anti-corruption stance; climate advocacy; resigned

former_leaders.name: Hammer DeRoburt
former_leaders.notes: Founding president; independence leader; negotiated phosphate control from BPC; invested revenues (poorly); London investments; dominant figure 21 years across three terms; died 1992; founding father
